clue.text: Brightness shown by English in old Welsh county briefly

indicators.note: briefly means the county name is cut short, keeping only its opening letters
in places one letter inside the shortened county name

blocks.note: Glamorgan was a historic county of south Wales
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Something brilliant attributed to an Englishman living in old Glamorgan.
explanation.walkthrough: Glamorgan shortened to GLAM, with E slipped in after GL, gives GLEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a brief flash of light, so it is a kind of brightness.

clue.text: Having set up gear, learner cooked, entertaining new sweetheart

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is raised, so it reads from bottom to top
entertaining means holding a guest within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a rig is a set of equipment or gear
L is for learner, as on L-plates
fried is one way food is cooked
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone sets up their kit while a learner cooks dinner for a new love.
explanation.walkthrough: RIG turned upwards is GIR; then L, then FRIED holding N gives FRIEND.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetheart is a romantic partner, which is what a girlfriend is.

clue.text: Coin once used in City University

blocks.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: An old coin that was once accepted on a university campus in the City.
explanation.walkthrough: EC (East Central) is the London postal district covering the City, the capital's financial square mile.
explanation.definitionFit: The ecu was an old French silver coin, and later the European currency unit before the euro.

clue.text: Frenchwoman’s mother in West?

indicators.note: in places the parent word inside the actress's first name

blocks.note: Mae West was a famous American film actress
a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: A puzzle about whether a French lady's mother lives out west.
explanation.walkthrough: West looks like a direction, but it points to the actress Mae West, around whom the mother word sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is the French title for a married woman, so it can stand for a Frenchwoman.

clue.text: Tree harsh old American disposed of in a song

indicators.note: disposed of says those letters are thrown away from the harsh word
in places the shortened harsh word inside the phrase a song

blocks.note: taken as written
a raucous sound is harsh and loud
O is the abbreviation for old
US is short for American, as in the United States
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A tree loses a harsh-voiced old American who is singing a song beneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: Disposed of applies to old and American, which both leave the harsh word; the tree is the monkey puzzle's genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Araucaria is the genus of conifers that includes the monkey puzzle tree.

clue.text: Toothless type in drama oddly having the Italian look

indicators.note: oddly means the letters are arranged in a strange way, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
il is the Italian word for the
lo is an old exclamation meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A gummy character in a play who has an Italian appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: Oddly might suggest taking odd letters, but here it rearranges the whole word. Armadillos were classed with the edentates, the toothless mammals.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo belongs to the old order Edentata, meaning without teeth, so it is a toothless type of animal.

clue.text: Seize woman not fully identified

blocks.note: Anne is a woman's name
X stands for someone whose name is withheld, as in Mrs X

explanation.surface: Grab a lady whose identity remains only half known.
explanation.walkthrough: A woman known only as Anne X is not fully identified: her surname is replaced by the unknown X.
explanation.definitionFit: To annex territory is to take possession of it by force, which is to seize it.

clue.text: Deceive a few about source of mulligatawny soup

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the opening letter is wanted
about means going around, so one word surrounds the letter

blocks.note: to con someone is to deceive them
some means a few
the first letter of mulligatawny

explanation.surface: Someone passes off a little curry soup as something else.
explanation.walkthrough: Mulligatawny looks like part of the definition, since it is a soup, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Consommé is a clear soup made from concentrated meat or fish stock.

clue.text: Highly populated like Lincoln? Not initially

indicators.note: not initially tells you to drop the opening letter of the word

blocks.note: Abraham Lincoln was a US president, so anything like him is presidential

explanation.surface: A question about whether the city of Lincoln is crowded.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln looks like the English cathedral city, but it is the American president.
explanation.definitionFit: A residential area is one occupied mainly by housing, so it is thickly settled with people.

clue.text: Supporter missing start of political gathering

indicators.note: missing start of means the opening letter is lost

blocks.note: a rally is a large political meeting

explanation.surface: A party loyalist who fails to turn up to the start of a political event.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is someone who backs you, a friend or partner in a cause.

clue.text: Sports club employee: no good? He delivers

indicators.note: no here means without, so the letter for good is taken away

blocks.note: a groundsman looks after a sports ground
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A club worker who is useless at his job, though he does deliver.
explanation.walkthrough: A roundsman is a British term for a tradesman who delivers along a regular round, such as a milkman.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundsman makes deliveries on a fixed route, like a milkman or baker's van driver.

clue.text: Twangy start to accompaniment disturbing northern girl

indicators.note: the start to a word is its first letter
disturbing means breaking into, so the letter is pushed inside

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
the first letter of accompaniment
Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally

explanation.surface: A twangy guitar backing upsets a girl from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A twangy voice has a resonant tone produced through the nose.

clue.text: Novelist’s crazed beast caught between two similar crossings

indicators.note: caught between means held in the middle of two other parts

blocks.note: a ford is a shallow river crossing, and two alike gives the same word twice
mad means crazed
an ox is a beast of burden

explanation.surface: A writer's mad animal gets stuck between two identical river crossings.
explanation.definitionFit: Ford Madox Ford was an English writer, author of The Good Soldier and Parade's End.

clue.text: Songbird enveloped at first in brightly-coloured flags

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word before it
in places that letter inside the colour word

blocks.note: red is a bright colour
the first letter of enveloped
bunting is a string of small flags used as decoration

explanation.surface: A bird is found wrapped up in a string of colourful flags.
explanation.walkthrough: Bunting is both flags and a family of birds, which helps the surface hang together.
explanation.definitionFit: The reed bunting is a small European bird of reedbeds, and it sings.

clue.text: I manage to catch CO and son overturning electron camera

indicators.note: overturning turns the word upside down, so in a down entry it reads upward
to catch means to hold something inside, so the I and manage words wrap round

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to capture a commanding officer and his son, who are toppling over.
explanation.walkthrough: I COPE holds CO plus SON turned up (NOS). CO is the usual abbreviation for commanding officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The iconoscope was an early television camera tube that scanned an image with an electron beam.

clue.text: Couple taken in some time after retirement

indicators.note: taken in means held within the following words
retirement is withdrawing, going back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters in the middle of these words

explanation.surface: A pair moves in together some time after one of them retires.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people romantically involved are informally called an item.

clue.text: Poor American lad losing heart, like some senior councillors

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter is removed
poor means in bad shape, so the letters are in disorder and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poor American boy, dispirited, behaves like an elderly council member.
explanation.walkthrough: LAD loses its middle A to leave LD, which joins AMERICAN for rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldermanic means relating to an alderman, a senior member of a borough or county council.

clue.text: Celebrate wildly, being suitable for putting up

indicators.note: wildly means in an uncontrolled way, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Throwing a wild party because something is fit to be built.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be erected, like a tent or shelf, can be put up.

clue.text: Main feature of gundog, away in Scotland for first time?

indicators.note: for first time means replacing the first T, a letter standing for time

blocks.note: a setter is a breed of gundog
awa is the Scots form of away

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a hunting dog's main trait when it heads off to Scotland for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: Time gives T, so for first time means swap the first T of SETTER. The main is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main, meaning the ocean, is made up of salt water, its defining feature.

clue.text: Aristocrats, small number moved by current sign

blocks.note: No is the short form of number
something blown along by a current of air is moved by it
an omen is a sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: Members of the upper class, a few of them touched by a passing trend.
explanation.definitionFit: Noblewomen are female members of the nobility, the aristocratic class.

clue.text: Celebrity using half of capital touring India

indicators.note: half of means only part of the word survives, the other part dropped
touring means travelling around, so the letters go round another

blocks.note: London is the capital of the UK
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A famous person half-based in the capital goes on a tour of India.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of LONDON is LON, which goes round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A lion, as in literary lion, is a much sought-after famous person.

clue.text: Like flying birds circling new canvas sunshade

indicators.note: circling means going round, so one word surrounds a letter

blocks.note: awing is an old word for on the wing, in flight
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Birds wheel round above a canvas shade.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a sheet of canvas stretched over a frame to keep sun or rain off.

clue.text: Untried bridge-player with drinks in antipodean state

blocks.note: something new has not been tried yet
the four bridge players are named North, East, South and West
W is the abbreviation for with
ales are beers

explanation.surface: A novice card player having a few drinks in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: New South Wales is a state in south-east Australia, a country in the antipodes.

clue.text: Bracing air a person found round most of animal park

indicators.note: most of means the word is cut short by its final letter
round means surrounding, so one word goes outside the other

blocks.note: one means a person, as in one should
a zoo is a park where animals are kept

explanation.surface: A visitor to a wildlife park gets a breath of fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: One for a person is a common crossword equivalence, as in one does one's best.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is used loosely for the fresh, invigorating air of the seaside.

clue.text: Time to get up and do the press chief’s job

indicators.note: in a down entry, to get up means rising from the bottom, so the word reads upward

blocks.note: tide is an old word for time, as in Yuletide

explanation.surface: Time for a newspaper boss to rise and get on with work.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief of a newspaper is its editor, whose job is to edit.

clue.text: Tenor taking break with daughter

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: A singer goes on holiday with his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Tenor looks like the singer, but it means general meaning, as in the tenor of a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The drift of an argument is its general meaning or gist, also called its tenor.

clue.text: Peculiar to a big lob, it’s essential to the score

indicators.note: peculiar means odd or strange, so the letters are put in an unusual order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tennis or cricket commentator finds a big lob strangely vital to the score.
explanation.walkthrough: Score looks like the result of a game, but it is a piece of written music.
explanation.definitionFit: An obbligato is a musical part that must not be left out, so it is an indispensable element of the score.

clue.text: Reportedly next in line’s bearing

indicators.note: reportedly means as said out loud, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

blocks.note: the next in line to inherit is the heir

explanation.surface: The way the heir to the throne carries himself.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a person's manner or demeanour, as is bearing.

clue.text: Girls originally employed in banks look at ornamental gem

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so only the first letter is wanted
employed in means put to work inside, so the letter goes within

blocks.note: banks can be tiers or rows, as of seats or keys
the first letter of girls
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: Young women working in banks admire a decorative jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: Banks suggests financial institutions, but here it means rows or tiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger's eye is a golden-brown striped quartz used in jewellery and decoration.

clue.text: Travel about carrying small shrub

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so one piece is inside another

blocks.note: to go is to travel
re means about or concerning
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Travelling around carrying a little bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse is a spiny yellow-flowered evergreen bush, also called furze or whin.
